info.title: Pipsocket trading API
info.description: Hosted MT5 accounts behind an API. Every call is for one account, under `/v1/accounts/{account}`, with your workspace's API key in `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. One trade call is one MT5 trade request, sent once: fields are MT5's `MqlTradeRequest` with readable values.

parameters.name: account
parameters.description: The account's id, `acc_` and 26 characters, as the dashboard shows it.

get.description: The account's login, status and connection, and the balance, equity and margin from its terminal's last report (once a second). Read from the engine, not the terminal, so it answers while the terminal is away.

post.description: Sends one trade request (MT5's `TRADE_ACTION_DEAL` for `buy` and `sell`, `TRADE_ACTION_PENDING` for the rest) to the account's terminal, with the stop loss and take profit in the same request, and waits up to 5 seconds for the trade server's answer. The request goes as you send it: nothing is split, retried, rounded or adjusted.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description:
Your own key for this request, 1 to 128 characters, not starting with `hk:` (Pipsocket's own
requests use that). A request with a key the account has used before (while that request is
kept: until 7 days after it settled) is not sent: the first request's answer comes back
instead, as it stands now.

200.description: MT5 accepted the request: `completed`, `placed` or `partial`, as the retcode says. Or, for the same `Idempotency-Key` sent again, a request settled as `executed`. A rejection answers 422 `trade_rejected`.

value.message: The request was completed.

202.description: No answer from the trade server within 5 seconds: the request is `pending` and is never sent again. Look it up to see how it ended. The same `Idempotency-Key` sent again answers 202 while the request is `pending` or `unknown`.

value.message: No answer from the trade server yet. The order may still execute; it is not sent again.

unknown.summary: The same key again, its request with no answer in time

value.message: The trade server's answer has not arrived in time. Until its outcome is known it blocks conflicting trades on its symbol; it settles when the terminal reports the answer, when the account's records show it, or when the account's owner settles it after checking the broker.

409.description:
- `symbol_busy`: An earlier request on the same symbol that this one would conflict with has no outcome yet (`blocking` lists them). Nothing was sent (`not_sent`). One still waiting for the trade server clears within seconds: retry after `Retry-After`. An `unknown` one blocks until its outcome is known: look it up instead of retrying.
- `not_executed`: The key's request was `unknown`, and was settled as never executed: by the terminal's own records, or by the account's owner after checking the broker (`settlement` says which). An owner's finding can be wrong: check positions and history before sending a new request, with a new `Idempotency-Key`.

Retry-After.description: 1, when every blocking request is still waiting for the trade server. Left out when one is `unknown`: look it up rather than retry.

not_executed.summary: The key's request was `unknown`, and was settled as never executed: by the terminal's own records, or by the account's owner after checking the broker (`settlement` says which). 422.description:
- `invalid_request`: A field, query parameter or header is missing, malformed or not allowed, or the body is not JSON. Nothing was sent.
- `magic_reserved`: `magic` is in the range Pipsocket keeps for its TradingView hooks' orders (2^52 to 2^53 - 1). Nothing was sent.
- `trade_rejected`: MT5 rejected the request: `result.retcode` says why. The body is the request, recorded with its id. It is final: change the request before sending it again, with a new `Idempotency-Key`.

AccountView.description:
The account, from the engine and its terminal's last report. Figures from the terminal are null
until it has reported.

status.description:
What the engine knows of the account's terminal: `starting`, `connected`, `disconnected`,
`unreachable` (the broker's server can't be reached; it keeps trying), `stopped`, or a status
someone has to act on: `auth_failed` (the broker refused the login), `server_not_found`,
`login_unknown` or `refused`.

connected.description: Whether the terminal reports a connection to the trade server.

trade_allowed.description:
Whether MT5 lets this terminal trade: the terminal, the account and automated trading all allow
it. False for an investor (read-only) login.

server_time.description: The trade server's time at the last report: broker server time, seconds since 1970.

Action.description:
MT5's `ENUM_TRADE_REQUEST_ACTIONS`: `deal` (`TRADE_ACTION_DEAL`, a market order or a close),
`pending` (`TRADE_ACTION_PENDING`), `sltp` (`TRADE_ACTION_SLTP`, a position's stops), `modify`
(`TRADE_ACTION_MODIFY`, a pending order's levels), `remove` (`TRADE_ACTION_REMOVE`, cancel a pending
order) and `close_by` (`TRADE_ACTION_CLOSE_BY`).

Blocking.description: A request this one waited for.

request.description: Its id: look it up with `GET /requests/{request}`.

state.description:
`pending` (waiting for the trade server) or `unknown` (no answer in time; it blocks until its
outcome is known).

retcode.description: MT5's return code: 0 when the check passed.

retcode_name.description: The return code's name; `UNKNOWN` for a code MT5 doesn't document.

profit.description: The floating profit after the trade.

margin_free.description: The free margin after the trade.

margin_level.description: The margin level after the trade, in percent.

CheckView.description: MT5's dry run (`OrderCheck`) of an order.

message.description: The return code's meaning, in a sentence.

CloseBy.description: Closing a position against an opposite one on the same symbol.

ClosePosition.description: Closing all or part of a position: a deal the other way naming the position.

volume.description: Lots to close: the position's whole volume, or part of it.

type_filling.description: How the closing deal may fill. Required: each symbol allows its own modes (its `filling_modes`).

price.description:
Sent as given (0 if left out): brokers with instant or request execution need it, those with
market or exchange execution ignore it.

deviation.description: The largest difference from `price` MT5 accepts, in points, for instant or request execution.

magic.description: Your own number, kept by MT5 on the closing deal.

comment.description: Up to 31 characters, kept by MT5 on the closing deal.

order.description: The order that made the deal.

entry.description: MT5's `DEAL_ENTRY`: `in` opens or adds, `out` closes, `inout` reverses, `out_by` closes by an opposite position.

reason.description: MT5's `DEAL_REASON`: who or what made the deal (`expert` for the API, `sl`, `tp`, `so` for a stop out).

EngageKillSwitch.description:
Engaging the kill switch may carry the deviation (in points) for its closing deals, which brokers
with instant or request execution need; MT5's empty value, 0, otherwise.

deviation.description:
The largest difference from the current price the closing deals accept, in points, for
instant or request execution. 0 if left out.

ErrorBody.description:
A refusal: a code to act on, and a message for people. Nothing else, so a recorded request (which
also has `error` and `message`) never fits it.

error.description: What went wrong, as a stable code.

message.description: What went wrong, for people. Its wording may change.

Filling.description:
MT5's `ENUM_ORDER_TYPE_FILLING`: `fok` (`ORDER_FILLING_FOK`, all or nothing), `ioc`
(`ORDER_FILLING_IOC`, what is available now, the rest cancelled), `return` (`ORDER_FILLING_RETURN`,
what is available now, the rest left as an order) and `boc` (`ORDER_FILLING_BOC`, book or cancel).
Each symbol allows its own modes: see `filling_modes` on the symbol.

HandSettlement.description: An unknown request settled by the account's owner or an admin, after checking the broker.

reason.description: What they found at the broker.

HistoryOrderView.description: An order no longer pending (MT5's `ORDER_*` history properties).

KillSwitchNotConnected.description: The kill switch engaged, but the terminal did not answer, so nothing was closed.

KillSwitchOutcome.description: What engaging the kill switch did.

flat.description:
No positions or pending orders in a fresh read of the account, and no trade that could add
exposure without a known outcome (`unknown` included).

cancelled.description: Each pending order and the removal sent for it (or the one already waiting for its answer).

closed.description: Each position and the close sent for it (or the one already waiting for its answer).

oneOf.description: What a fresh read found afterwards; null if the terminal did not answer it.

unanswered.description:
Ids of requests sent before the switch engaged that could add exposure and have no known
outcome. If one fills and the terminal reports it, the switch closes what it opened.

message.description: What the outcome means, in a sentence.

KillSwitchUnavailable.description:
Engaging the kill switch answered 503: either a refusal before the engine, or the switch engaged
while the terminal did not answer.

KillSwitchView.description: Whether the account's kill switch is engaged.

since.description: When it was engaged: seconds since 1970 (UTC). Null when it is not engaged.

deviation.description: The deviation, in points, its closing deals carry. Null when it is not engaged.

ModifyOrder.description:
A pending order's new levels. `price`, `sl`, `tp` and `type_time` are all required, as MT5 replaces
every level: give the ones you keep as they are.

price.description: The price the order waits for.

stoplimit.description:
Required when the order is a stop-limit order: the price of the limit order placed once `price`
is reached.

expiration.description:
When the order expires: broker server time, seconds since 1970. Required for `type_time`
`specified` and `specified_day`.

position.description: The position the order belongs to, if any.

PlaceOrder.description:
A market or pending order. Fields left out are sent as MT5's empty values (0, "", `gtc`); there is
no other default. Fields not listed here are refused.

symbol.description: The symbol exactly as the broker names it, such as `EURUSD`.

type.description:
What to send. `buy` and `sell` fill now; the others wait at `price`. `close_by` is refused here:
use Close by.

volume.description: Lots. MT5 rejects a volume outside the symbol's minimum, maximum and step.

type_filling.description: How the order may fill. Required: each symbol allows its own modes (its `filling_modes`).

price.description:
Required for pending orders: the price the order waits for. For a market order it is sent as
given (0 if left out): brokers with instant or request execution need it, those with market or
exchange execution ignore it.

stoplimit.description:
Required for `buy_stop_limit` and `sell_stop_limit`: the price of the limit order placed once
`price` is reached.

sl.description: Stop loss price, set in the same request. 0 or left out: none.

tp.description: Take profit price, set in the same request. 0 or left out: none.

deviation.description: The largest difference from `price` MT5 accepts, in points, for instant or request execution.

type_time.description: How long a pending order lasts. `gtc` if left out.

expiration.description:
When a pending order expires: broker server time, seconds since 1970. Required for `type_time`
`specified` and `specified_day`.

magic.description: Your own number for the order, kept by MT5 on the order, its deals and its position.

comment.description: Up to 31 characters, kept by MT5 on the order. Brokers may replace it.

PositionLevels.description:
A position's stop loss and take profit. Both are required, as MT5 sets both: give the one you keep
as it is.

ticket.description: The position's ticket: use it to close the position or set its stops.

identifier.description: The position's id, which stays the same if the broker changes the ticket.

time_msc.description: When it was opened: broker server time, milliseconds since 1970.

RequestState.description:
A trade request's state. MT5 answered: `completed` (`TRADE_RETCODE_DONE`, 10009), `placed`
(`TRADE_RETCODE_PLACED`, 10008), `partial` (`TRADE_RETCODE_DONE_PARTIAL`, 10010) or `rejected`
(any other retcode, from the trade server or from the terminal refusing to send it). No answer
yet: `pending` (sent, never sent again) or `unknown` (no answer within 130 seconds: it may have
executed, so it blocks conflicting trades on its symbol until its outcome is known). `not_sent`:
the terminal did not send it. For one that was `unknown`: `not_executed` or `executed`, as
`settlement` says who found it.

RequestView.description: A trade request: the request as recorded for the terminal (`sent`), its state, and MT5's answer.

request.description: The request's id (`req_...`): look it up with `GET /requests/{request}`.

oneOf.description:
MT5's `MqlTradeResult` once MT5 answered; why it was not sent once `not_sent` or
`not_executed`; who settled it and why, when the account's owner did; otherwise null.

message.description: What the answer means, in a sentence.

error.description: Set when the request did not go through: `trade_rejected`, `not_sent` or `not_executed`.

Settlement.description:
Who settled an `unknown` request: `evidence` (the terminal's own records prove it never passed
the request to MT5) or `operator` (the account's owner or an admin, after checking the broker:
their finding, which can be wrong; `result` says who and why).

SymbolBusy.description:
409 `symbol_busy`: requests on the same symbol that this one would conflict with have no outcome
yet, so it was not sent.

not_sent.description: Always true: this call was not submitted.

SymbolSummaryView.description:
A symbol in the list (MT5's `SYMBOL_*` properties). Properties are read without adding the symbol to
Market Watch, so an unavailable one has empty values.

path.description: Where it sits in the broker's symbol tree.

available.description: Whether the terminal could read its properties.

trading.description: MT5's `SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE`: whether and which way the symbol can be traded.

in_market_watch.description: Whether it is in the terminal's Market Watch.

SymbolView.description: A symbol's specification (MT5's `SYMBOL_*` properties), with its mode flags spelled out.

available.description: Whether the terminal could read its properties; when false the rest are empty values.

stops_level.description: The closest stops may be to the price, in points.

freeze_level.description: How close to the price an order or stop is frozen, in points.

filling_mode.description: MT5's flags, as `filling_modes` spells them out.

trade_mode.description: MT5's value, as `trading` spells it out.

execution_mode.description: MT5's value, as `execution` spells it out.

order_mode.description: MT5's flags, as `order_types` spells them out.

expiration_mode.description: MT5's flags, as `expirations` spells them out.

filling_modes.description: The `type_filling` modes MT5's `SYMBOL_FILLING_MODE` flags allow. `return` has no flag: whether it is accepted depends on the symbol's execution and the broker.

execution.description: MT5's `SYMBOL_TRADE_EXEMODE`. Instant and request execution need `price` (and use `deviation`).

trading.description: MT5's `SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE`: whether and which way the symbol can be traded.

TickView.description:
A symbol's latest tick (MT5's `MqlTick`). `time_msc`, `last`, `volume` and `flags` are null from
terminals on bridges older than 2.02.

TradeConflict.description:
A trade call answered 409: either `symbol_busy` (nothing was sent or recorded), or a stored request
settled as never executed (`not_executed`).

TradeRejected.description:
A trade call answered 422: either a refusal (nothing was sent or recorded), or a stored request MT5
rejected (`trade_rejected`).

TradeRequest.description:
MT5's `MqlTradeRequest`, field for field, exactly as recorded to send to the terminal: the
request's `state` and `result` say whether it reached MT5. Fields the call does not use carry MT5's
empty values (0, "", `fok`, `gtc`).

symbol.description: The symbol, exactly as the broker names it.

price.description: The price: a pending order's, or the one instant and request execution trade at.

stoplimit.description: A stop-limit order's limit price, placed once `price` is reached.

deviation.description: The largest difference from `price` MT5 accepts, in points.

type_time.description: How long a pending order lasts.

expiration.description: Broker server time, seconds since 1970, as MT5 takes it.

order.description: The pending order the request is about (modify, remove).

position.description: The position the request is about (close, stops, close by).

position_by.description: The opposite position, for close by.

magic.description: Your own number, kept by MT5 on the order, its deals and its position.

comment.description: Up to 31 characters, kept by MT5 on the order.

TradeResult.description: MT5's `MqlTradeResult`, as the trade server (or the terminal, refusing to send) answered.

retcode.description: MT5's return code: see Errors and retcodes.

retcode_name.description: The return code's name; `UNKNOWN` for a code MT5 doesn't document.

comment.description: The broker's comment on the answer.

order.description: The order's ticket, if one was placed.

deal.description: The deal's ticket, if one was made.

position.description: The position's ticket, where the trade server gives it.

bid.description: The bid when the request was handled (requotes).

ask.description: The ask when the request was handled (requotes).

retcode_external.description: The external trading system's code, if the broker routes to one.

TradeUnavailable.description:
A trade call answered 503: either a refusal (the request was not recorded), or a stored request the
terminal did not send (`not_sent`).

TypeTime.description:
MT5's `ENUM_ORDER_TYPE_TIME`: `gtc` (`ORDER_TIME_GTC`, until cancelled), `day` (`ORDER_TIME_DAY`,
the trading day), `specified` (`ORDER_TIME_SPECIFIED`, until `expiration`) and `specified_day`
(`ORDER_TIME_SPECIFIED_DAY`, until the end of `expiration`'s day).

api_key.description: Your workspace's API key (`psk_...`), from the dashboard's API key page.

errors.meaning: No API key: send it as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.
The key is not a workspace's current key (a rolled key stops working within about a minute).
No such account, or one the key's workspace doesn't have: the two look the same.
The account has no pending order with that ticket (read fresh from the terminal).
The account has no open position with that ticket (read fresh from the terminal).
The account has no request with that id (a request is kept 7 days after its outcome is known).
The broker has no symbol by that name.
A field, query parameter or header is missing, malformed or not allowed, or the body is not JSON. Nothing was sent.
`magic` is in the range Pipsocket keeps for its TradingView hooks' orders (2^52 to 2^53 - 1). Nothing was sent.
MT5 rejected the request: `result.retcode` says why. The body is the request, recorded with its id. It is final: change the request before sending it again, with a new `Idempotency-Key`.

The key's request was `unknown`, and was settled as never executed: by the terminal's own records, or by the account's owner after checking the broker (`settlement` says which). An owner's finding can be wrong: check positions and history before sending a new request, with a new `Idempotency-Key`.

An earlier request on the same symbol that this one would conflict with has no outcome yet (`blocking` lists them). Nothing was sent (`not_sent`). One still waiting for the trade server clears within seconds: retry after `Retry-After`. An `unknown` one blocks until its outcome is known: look it up instead of retrying.
The history range holds more than one answer can carry: ask for a shorter range.
The account's kill switch is engaged: new orders and changes to pending orders are refused until it is lifted. Nothing was sent.

The account is close-only because the workspace's payment is overdue: new orders and changes to pending orders are refused until the payment goes through (update the card on the dashboard's Billing page). Lifting the kill switch doesn't lift it. Nothing was sent.

The account's terminal is not connected to the engine (stopped, starting, or restarting). Nothing was sent, except by the kill switch: engaging it still engages it, and may already have deleted pending orders.
The account's terminal runs an older bridge that can't trade: restart the account to update it. Nothing was sent.
The account's terminal is being replaced. Nothing was sent; try again in a minute.

The terminal did not send the request, for example `busy` with 1,000 trades already waiting for the trade server (`result.error` says why). The body is the request, recorded with its id, and the same `Idempotency-Key` answers it again: send it again with a new key.
The terminal refused the command, for example a negative `expiration`, or a history range MT5 can't select.
The terminal did not give the answer asked for.
One symbol's entry is too large for the terminal to list.
The terminal has no price for the symbol yet (it waited 2 seconds).
The account's engine host has too many calls in flight (256). Nothing was done; try again.
The account's engine host is not connected to Pipsocket, or disconnected while the call waited. A trade it already had is still settled: look it up.
The account's terminal did not answer within 5 seconds.
The account's engine did not answer within 30 seconds.
